purpose: Screening pass to identify I-SPY2 cases with a UNILATERAL (single-breast) MRI field of view, as opposed to the BILATERAL (both-breasts-in-frame) FOV that the ambl training dataset always uses. A unilateral scan is a fundamentally different acquisition/FOV protocol, not just a different contrast, and is excluded from any prediction/evaluation of ambl-trained models on I-SPY2 to avoid conflating protocol-level distribution shift with the cross-contrast shift this cross-eval dataset is meant to isolate.
generated_by: manual screening pass (see METHOD below); does NOT modify or delete any underlying I-SPY2 data files, and is NOT wired into any evaluation config -- a separate effort owns using this list.
source_of_truth: datasets/ispy2/0_raw_ispy2/ispy2_final_manifest.csv (column dce_desc, e.g. 'ISPY2: VOLSER: uni-lateral cropped: original DCE' vs 'ISPY2: VOLSER: bi-lateral: original DCE') -- this is the TCIA/site-level DICOM SeriesDescription of the VOLSER-reconstructed DCE series actually used to build this project's BIDS conversion, i.e. an acquisition/reconstruction-pipeline field, not a derived heuristic.

method.1_metadata: Primary signal: ispy2_final_manifest.csv's dce_desc field, already used during onboarding (see datasets/ispy2/0_raw_ispy2/README.md) to report 443 uni-lateral / 118 bi-lateral of 561 total. Directly re-derived here: 442 uni-lateral / 118 bi-lateral among the 560 cases that actually have BIDS data (1 of the 443 has no BIDS conversion at all, see no_bids_data below).
method.2_geometric_corroboration: For every one of the 560 available cases, computed the physical left-right FOV width (shape[0] * pixdim[0] on the LPS-oriented acq-firstpost_T1w.nii.gz, axis 0 = L per nib.aff2axcodes) and a breast-symmetry 'balance' metric (foreground mass profile along the L-R axis, split at its central valley, ratio of the smaller to larger side peak). FOV width alone separates the two metadata groups almost perfectly (unilateral-tagged median 178.9mm, range 130-360mm; bilateral-tagged median 330mm, range 290-440mm; only 3/560 cases fall in the numeric overlap zone).
method.3_manual_visual_audit: The 'balance' profile metric flagged 39 uni-lateral-tagged cases as geometrically symmetric (balance>=0.65, i.e. candidate mislabels) and 4 bi-lateral-tagged cases as asymmetric (balance<0.65). ALL 43 were individually visually inspected (mid-gland + additional axial slices of the first-post-contrast T1w volume, rendered as PNG contact sheets). Findings: (a) the 4 bilateral-tagged/low-balance cases were all confirmed genuinely bilateral -- the low balance score there was just an artifact of asymmetric contrast enhancement between the two breasts, not a laterality error; no changes made. (b) Of the 39 unilateral-tagged/high-balance candidates, 35 were FALSE POSITIVES of the balance metric -- caused by a small bright round marker/lymph-node structure near the single breast being counted as a second 'peak' by the profile algorithm; visual inspection confirmed these are genuinely single-breast images and metadata is correct. The remaining 4 (ISPY2-208265, ISPY2-627981, ISPY2-229144, ISPY2-318293) were confirmed on visual inspection to genuinely show BOTH breasts despite the 'uni-lateral cropped' pipeline tag -- these are corrected overrides, kept as usable bilateral cases, NOT excluded.
method.conclusion: The raw metadata tag, taken alone, has a small (4/442, ~0.9%) false-exclusion rate for cases where the 'uni-lateral cropped' reconstruction pipeline was applied but still retained both breasts in frame. The naive geometric 'balance' metric alone is NOT reliable as a standalone classifier (majority of its unilateral-vs-bilateral disagreements with metadata were false positives from bright marker/node artifacts, not real laterality differences) -- it was used only as a triage tool to flag the ~7% of cases worth a manual look, and manual visual inspection was the final arbiter for every flagged case. FOV width was the most consistent corroborating signal, agreeing with the final (metadata + 4 overrides) classification for 557/560 cases (99.5%).
